name: Abel
charge: Bringing the firstlings of his flock and the fat thereof
summary: The first offering scripture records as accepted, and the first man it calls righteous. Abel brought the firstlings and the fat, and the Lord had respect unto him. His brother's envy killed him, and his blood still speaks.
offense: Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain: the first and the best, not the leftover, and brought in faith. The law of the firstlings and the fat was written later; Abel kept it before it was written.
judgment: The Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering. By it he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh. Christ names him righteous Abel, the first of the prophets whose blood was shed. His blessing is a standing before God that outlasted his life.

text.text: And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.
And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:
But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.
By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.
That thou shalt set apart unto the Lord all that openeth the matrix, and every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast; the males shall be the Lord’s.
And the priest shall burn them upon the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire for a sweet savour: all the fat is the Lord’s.
Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.
